newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends weaker on strong stg, origins.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends weaker on strong stg, origins.

text.p: London cocoa futures ended softer on Tuesday as strong sterling kept origin selling lively, although afternoon dealings centred mainly on crosses.
Traders said there was little news to cling on to while London failed to follow a marginal recovery in New York.
"This market doesn't move up. It doesn't move down. The direction is all over the place," said one trader.
The benchmark March contract ended five stg down at 992 stg a tonne, off a session low of 988 stg while spot December slid six stg to 965 stg.
Volume totalled 5,396 lots but traders reckoned some 2,441 lots were crossed, including 300 lots of September at 1,030 stg.
On the switches, May/Sept traded at 28 stg, March/July at 25 abd March/Sept at 40 stg, traders said.
Eyes are on Ivory Coast which has yet to fix its farm gate prices despite an official opening set for Tuesday. But traders say there may be a delay of about a week.
Such delays are not unusual and analysts reckon there will be enough supplies coming in the last quarter of this year.

One crop forecaster said earlier a total Ivorian harvest this season of one million tonnes was very feasible. This would compare with last season's record crop of 1.2 million tonnes and forecasts earlier this year of around 800,000-900,000 tonnes.
The crop was expected to peak around November or early December, although December could be relatively poor compared with last year. They would pick up again after that.
Technical support is seen at 985 stg on March. Resistance is pegged at 1,000 and 1,025.
